raw_annotations.proposed_function: N-terminal intrinsically disordered region (IDR) involved in binding to the A48 aptamer and maintaining efficient interaction/structural dynamics.
raw_annotations.evidence: Previous studies have indicated the importance of the basic finger region of N-NTD for RNA/DNA binding. However, those studies used a truncated form of N-NTD lacking the N-terminal IDR (residues 1–43) [2,24–26].

raw_annotations.proposed_function: N-terminal IDR segment showing newly observed signals or substantial chemical shift changes upon A48 binding, indicating specific recognition.
raw_annotations.evidence: Residues G30–S51 (N-terminal IDR) and T91–K102 (basic finger region) showed either newly observed signals or substantial chemical shift changes (chemical shift variation > 0.3 ppm).

raw_annotations.proposed_function: Critical segment within the N-terminal IDR mediating A48 binding, as deletion of this region reduces binding affinity.
raw_annotations.evidence: This observation highlights the critical role of residues S26–Q43 within the N-terminal IDR in mediating A48 binding, a conclusion supported by backbone chemical shift variation (CSV) analysis.

raw_annotations.proposed_function: Basic finger region (part of N-NTD) involved in A48 binding, showing substantial spectral changes and containing Arg residues that interact with the aptamer.
raw_annotations.evidence: Residues G30–S51 (N-terminal IDR) and T91–K102 (basic finger region) showed either newly observed signals or substantial chemical shift changes (chemical shift variation > 0.3 ppm).
